content.text:
**Verdict: keep ours, borrow two things. Nothing surveyed replaces it.**

Every alternative is a generic *session/agent* monitor. None joins events to a plan. Our board's whole value is the join: `PROGRESS.md` lanes → boxes ← hook events. Swapping loses that; adding one alongside doubles hook cost (each hook spawns a node process) for a second copy of the same stream.

## What each one is

| project | shape | plan model | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| [claude-code-kanban](https://github.com/NikiforovAll/claude-code-kanban) (CCK) | Node + SSE, 20k LOC, plugin hooks | Claude's native `TaskCreate` files (`~/.claude/tasks`). Flat, per-session, off by default on Opus 5 (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS`) | no — flat list vs our milestone→step→lane→box; second writer to plan state |
| [Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor](https://github.com/hoangsonww/Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor) (CCAM) | Express + SQLite + React + WS + Electron + MCP + Codex, **168k LOC** | "kanban" = agents/sessions by Working/Waiting/Completed. Task progress reduced from `TodoWrite` in transcripts | no — product, not a viewer; board columns are agent status, not work |
| [agents-observe](https://github.com/simple10/agents-observe) | Hono + SQLite + React, Docker | none — event stream only | no — same as our Activity tail, heavier |
| [disler observability](https://github.com/disler/claude-code-hooks-multi-agent-observability) | hook → HTTP → WS, swimlanes | none | no — we already have swimlanes |
| agent-platform (ours) | Rust server + iced native app | processes created by *its* planner, approved as DAG (`/processes/{id}/approve` takes `dag_json`); no external-run ingest; todos = product todo board | ADR 0001 rejection holds. Re-checked: still no seam to push Claude Code lanes in without copying |

## Worth borrowing from CCK (cheap → less cheap)

1. **Waiting state.** CCK hooks `PermissionRequest` (+ `AskUserQuestion`/`ExitPlanMode`) → `_waiting.json` marker → amber card; `PostToolUse` clears it. Our ADR names the gap: "busy agent can look idle for minutes" — and blocked-on-permission is indistinguishable from generating. Add `PermissionRequest` + `Notification` to [settings.local.json](.claude/settings.local.json), emit `agent.waiting` in [emit.py](.local/hooks/emit.py), clear on next `tool.post`, amber badge in page. ~20 lines across three files.
2. **Assistant text in the detail sidebar.** CCK's "session log" renders prompts/replies from the transcript JSONL. [board.py](.local/board.py) already tails every subagent transcript for tokens; pulling the last assistant text out of the same tail shows what the agent is *saying* between tool calls. ~30 lines.

Skip:
- **UI approvals** (blocking `PermissionRequest` hook polling a decision file) — desktop app already has that UI. One design note worth keeping if we ever do: gate on `PermissionRequest`, not `PreToolUse` — TUI dialog freezes under a blocking `PreToolUse`.
- **Doorbell** (`monitors.json` `on-skill-invoke` → process prints lines → session gets task notifications). Board→session channel. Clever, but main thread already receives every subagent's report; nothing to deliver.
- **Statusline spy** (`context-status.sh | existing statusline`) for main-thread ctx/cost. Only if transcript-inferred ctx proves wrong; not so far.
- Themes, PWA, storage manager, keyboard shortcuts, teams idle detection.

Say go → I do 1 + 2, append a "surveyed 2026-09-15" note to [ADR 0001](.local/adr/0001-agent-board.md), republish. Want this as a page? One line and I'll publish it.

Sources: [claude-code-kanban](https://github.com/NikiforovAll/claude-code-kanban), [Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor](https://github.com/hoangsonww/Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor), [agents-observe](https://github.com/simple10/agents-observe), [disler/claude-code-hooks-multi-agent-observability](https://github.com/disler/claude-code-hooks-multi-agent-observability), [agents-observe writeup](https://www.blog.brightcoding.dev/2026/08/07/simple10agents-observe-real-time-dashboard-for-claude-code-sessions)

"Enhance CCAM" without forking = install it as a plugin *alongside* ours whenever you want its analytics/cost/notifications. Hooks are additive. That is the reversible path; a fork is not.

**Where:** `D:/projects/production/ai/plugins/board` — fourth entry in the `tanvoid0` marketplace beside governor/crew/hands. One `claude plugin install board@tanvoid0` → hooks fire in every project. (Alt: standalone repo. Marketplace wins: same install story as crew, one repo to version.)

# board — a plan-joined build board for Claude Code, across every project

- Status: proposed, 2026-09-15
- Decider: Tanveer Hoque
- Supersedes: `ledgerflow/.local/adr/0001-agent-board.md` (v2) and `ledgerflow/.local/board-spec.md`, which stay as the
  record of how the per-repo version was built and measured.

## 1. What this is

A Claude Code plugin. Hooks report what every agent in every project is doing; a stdlib Node server joins those events to
the project's plan (`PROGRESS.md`: milestones → steps → lanes → boxes) and serves one derived model; a single HTML page
renders it live over SSE and, published as an artifact, renders the same model as a snapshot. A skill teaches the main
thread the text API so it reads the board instead of the files.

Three rules carried over from v2, still load-bearing:

1. **The harness reports, not the agents.** Hooks are the source of every event. Box-level log lines from agents are
   optional refinement, never the signal.
2. **The server owns nothing.** Files are the truth; kill the server and nothing is lost. `PROGRESS.md` has one writer,
   the main thread (by hand or through `POST /tick`). That is what keeps four agents from colliding.
3. **The page parses nothing.** It renders the model and the raw event tail.

## 2. Why this and not one of the existing boards

Surveyed 2026-09-15:

| project | what it is | plan model | why not |
|---|---|---|---|
| [claude-code-kanban](https://github.com/NikiforovAll/claude-code-kanban) | Node + SSE viewer over `~/.claude`, 20k LOC, plugin hooks; waiting badges, UI approvals, board→session doorbell, 17 themes | Claude's native task files (`TaskCreate`), flat, per session, off by default on Opus 5 / Fable 5 | no hierarchy, no lanes, a second writer of plan state next to the markdown |
| [Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor](https://github.com/hoangsonww/Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor) | Express + SQLite + React + WebSockets + Electron + MCP + Codex, 168k LOC, 2,980-line ARCHITECTURE.md, 39 server libs, 18 tables | none — its kanban is agents/sessions by Working · Waiting · Completed; task progress is reduced from `TodoWrite` in transcripts | the plan join would be a new domain (tables, parser, join, tick, React pages) inside a codebase we do not know, diverging from a 1,010-commit upstream we could never pull again |
| [agents-observe](https://github.com/simple10/agents-observe) | Hono + SQLite + React, Docker; hook → HTTP → event stream | none | the same as our Activity tail, with a database and a container |
| [disler observability](https://github.com/disler/claude-code-hooks-multi-agent-observability) | hook → HTTP → WS, swimlanes, pulse chart | none | we have swimlanes |
| agent-platform (ours) | Rust server + iced desktop; processes are created by its planner and approved as a DAG (`/processes/{id}/approve` takes `dag_json`) | its own DAG | no seam to ingest an external run; Claude Code subagents cannot be routed through its proxy; its todos are a product todo board. ADR 0001 rejection stands. |

Every one of them is a generic session or agent monitor. The value here is the join — a box on a lane in a step of a
milestone, with the agent, its commands, its errors and its tokens attributed to it — and none of them has a plan to
join to. Forking the biggest one to add it would cost more than the whole of this, and cut us off from its upstream.

**"Enhance CCAM" without forking:** install it as a plugin next to this one whenever its analytics, cost reports or
notifications are wanted. Hooks are additive; two plugins see the same events. That door stays open. A fork closes it.

Borrowed, with credit: the waiting-state marker and its clearing rule (CCK), the transcript session log (CCK), the
`server.json` beacon (CCK), a per-model price table (CCK, CCAM, governor).

## 3. Shape

### 3.1 Where it lives

`D:/projects/production/ai/plugins/board` — the fourth plugin in the `tanvoid0` marketplace beside governor, crew and
hands. Install once, fires in every project:

```bash
claude plugin install board@tanvoid0
```

### 3.2 Runtime

Node, standard library only (`http`, `fs`, `path`, `os`). No `package.json` dependencies. Reasons: every plugin in the
marketplace is JS; a public hook plugin cannot assume Python on the host; Claude Code itself needs Node, so Node is
always there. The page is one HTML file and ports as-is.

### 3.3 Layout

```
board/
  .claude-plugin/plugin.json      name, version, description
  hooks/hooks.json                the events below, all routed to emit.js
  hooks/emit.js                   hook payload → one JSON line; exit 0 always, never fails the tool call
  server/board.js                 http + SSE + fs.watch; parses the plan, pools the log, joins events, tails transcripts
  server/prices.js                $ per million tokens by model id, four classes; unknown model → null cost
  page/index.html                 the renderer; served by the server and published as the artifact
  skills/board/SKILL.md           the text API and the conventions, for the main thread
  test/fixtures/<project>/        PROGRESS.md · log.md · events.jsonl · transcripts/ · expected summary.txt
  test/check.js                   node test/check.js — builds the model from every fixture, asserts the expected text
  docs/spec.md                    this file
  README.md
```

### 3.4 Data — where every byte goes

| path | writer | content |
|---|---|---|
| `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/.board/server.json` | server | `{"port": 8099, "pid": …}` beacon; written on start, removed on clean exit |
| `~/.claude/.board/<projEnc>/project.json` | `emit.js`, first event for that project | `{"cwd": "D:/projects/…/ledgerflow", "seen": "<iso>"}` |
| `~/.claude/.board/<projEnc>/events.jsonl` | `emit.js` | one JSON object per line, schema in §4 |
| `~/.claude/.board/<projEnc>/model.json` | server, atomic (tmp + rename), ≤ once per 2 s | the derived model, §5 |
| `<cwd>/PROGRESS.md` | main thread only | the plan, grammar in §6 |
| `<cwd>/.local/log.md` | agents (optional), main thread, `POST /log` | box-level lines, §6 |

`projEnc` is Claude Code's own project-directory encoding — every character that is not `[A-Za-z0-9]` becomes `-`
(`D:\projects\practice\microservices\ledgerflow` → `D--projects-practice-microservices-ledgerflow`). Using the same
key means `~/.claude/projects/<projEnc>/` (the transcripts) and `~/.claude/.board/<projEnc>/` (the events) pair by
name, and a session's `transcript_path` locates its project without a lookup.

The plugin writes nothing inside a project. The two project-local files are the user's conventions, edited by the
user's own main thread and agents (through the tick and log routes, or by hand); a project that has neither still
shows up on the board as agents and events, with no plan.

**Project discovery:** every `~/.claude/.board/<projEnc>/` directory. A project is *active* if it has an event in the
last 10 minutes, *recent* within 7 days, else *archived* (listed, not loaded until asked).

**Slug** (what the API and the picker use): the basename of `cwd`; when two projects share a basename, both become
`<parent>-<basename>`. `project.json` records the slug the server assigned so it never changes under a running session.

## 4. Hooks and the event schema

`hooks/hooks.json` registers `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/emit.js"` with a 5 s timeout for:

| hook | matcher | event emitted |
|---|---|---|
| `SessionStart` | — | `session.start` — also writes `project.json` if missing |
| `SessionEnd` | — | `session.end` |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | — | `turn.start` (`prompt` ≤ 200 chars) |
| `Stop` | — | `turn.stop` (the main thread's turn ended; the main is idle now, not "live for 10 more minutes") |
| `SubagentStart` | — | `agent.start` |
| `SubagentStop` | — | `agent.stop` |
| `PreToolUse` | `Bash\|Edit\|Write\|Read\|Grep\|Glob\|NotebookEdit\|Agent` | `tool.pre` |
| `PostToolUse` | `Bash\|Edit\|Write\|NotebookEdit` | `tool.post` |
| `PostToolUseFailure` | `Bash\|Edit\|Write\|NotebookEdit` | `tool.post` with `failed: true` |
| `PermissionRequest` | — | `agent.waiting` (`kind`: `permission`, or `question` for `AskUserQuestion`, `plan` for `ExitPlanMode`) |
| `Notification` | `permission_prompt\|idle_prompt` | `agent.waiting` (`kind`: `permission` / `idle`) — the belt to `PermissionRequest`'s braces; the server dedupes by agent |

`emit.js` is the v2 `emit.py` ported line for line, plus the six new events. It reads `cwd` and `transcript_path` from
the payload (falling back to `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`), derives `projEnc`, appends, exits 0. Every error is swallowed.

**Common fields** on every line: `ts` (UTC ISO ms), `cwd`, `session` (first 8 chars of the session id), `agent`
(17-char agent id, or `main`), `type` (`crew:coder` etc.; `agent` when the id had no type; `main`), `step` (the
`## Current step: N` of `<cwd>/PROGRESS.md`, if any), `ev`.

| `ev` | extra fields |
|---|---|
| `session.start` / `session.end` | — |
| `turn.start` | `prompt` (≤ 200 chars) |
| `turn.stop` | — |
| `agent.start` | `lane` (letter, when the prompt begins `Lane X`), `title` (text after `Lane X —`), `transcript` (absolute path of the subagent transcript — `<dir of transcript_path>/<session_id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, or `agent_transcript_path` when the payload carries it). The prompt is the first user line of that transcript, on disk ~100 ms before the hook fires; retry six times at 50 ms. |
| `agent.stop` | — |
| `agent.waiting` | `kind`, `tool`, `input` (≤ 200 chars of `tool_input`) |
| `tool.pre` | `tool`, `id` (tool_use_id); main thread only: `transcript` (the session transcript); Bash: `cmd` (≤ 400), `desc`; Edit/Write/Read/NotebookEdit: `file` (relative to `cwd`); Grep/Glob: `pattern`, `file`; Agent: `desc`, `subagent`, `lane`, `title` (parsed from the dispatch prompt) |
| `tool.post` | `tool`, `id`, `ms`; Bash: `out`, `err` (last 600 chars each), `interrupted`; a failed call arrives only through `PostToolUseFailure` → `failed: true`, `err` = the error text |

**Waiting is cleared, never toggled off by a hook:** the next `tool.pre`, `tool.post`, `agent.stop` or `turn.stop` by
the same agent clears it in the model. That is CCK's rule and it is the reason the badge cannot stick.

Lane attribution needs the dispatch prompt to start with `Lane X — <name>`. Anything else shows as `?` — honest,
and the signal that a dispatch went out without the convention. Unchanged from v2.

## 5. The derived model

`GET /api/<slug>/model`, SSE `event: model`, and `model.json`. The v2 shape, plus `project`, `waiting`, `say`, `cost`:

```jsonc
{
  "now": "iso",
  "project": {"slug": "ledgerflow", "cwd": "D:/…/ledgerflow", "projEnc": "D--projects-…", "active": true,
              "plan": true},                      // plan: <cwd>/PROGRESS.md exists and parsed
  "status": {"date": "2026-09-15", "text": "16 / 32 steps done · …"},
  "steps": {"done": 16, "total": 32, "current": 16},
  "milestones": [{"id": "M1", "title": "…", "done": true,
                  "steps": [{"num": "01", "title": "…", "done": true, "current": false, "commit": "3237c3a"}]}],
  "stories": [                                    // current step first, then sandboxes in file order
    {"id": "step-16", "kind": "step", "num": 16, "title": "…", "doneWhen": "…", "decisions": "<markdown>",
```

  first, then sandboxes). The main thread is lane `C` when the current step has one.

  blocked, `doing` if any child is doing/reported, else its own log-derived status. Counts include every depth.
- **task agent / times**: `agent` = label of the `start` line (else `done`); a label matches an agent when it equals

- **tool attribution**: the `start` line for KEY by label L opens a window closing at L's next later line that is
  another key's `start` or this key's `done`/`blocked`; `tool.pre` by a matching agent on that lane inside the window
  counts (`tools`; `errors` = `tool.post` with `err`, `failed` or `interrupted`).

- **NEW waiting**: set by `agent.waiting`; cleared by the agent's next `tool.pre` / `tool.post` / `agent.stop` /
  `turn.stop`; a `waiting` agent is still `live`.
- **Transcript tail** (per `transcript` path seen; byte offset kept in memory, whole file on first sight; dedupe
  `message.id`): `model` (last), `calls`, Σ of all four usage classes (**NEW**: `in`, `cw`, `cr` alongside `out`), `ctx`

4. Remove the `hooks` block from `.claude/settings.local.json` (otherwise every event is written twice); stop 8099;

- Generation time stays invisible; `say` shows the last thing that landed, not what is being written.
- A killed agent never gets `agent.stop`; it ages out after 30 min. A main thread whose `Stop` hook is lost ages out

- `events.jsonl` grows ~1 line per tool call. Rotate at a step boundary (`events.jsonl` → `events.<step>.jsonl`; the

- `turn.start.prompt` puts the first 200 chars of every user prompt into a file that gets published as an artifact

- `fs.watch` semantics differ per platform; the 1 s stat poll is the fallback and the SSE debounce hides it.

authentication (binds `127.0.0.1`), a hosted mode.

- In the marketplace repo, not a standalone repo.
- Events global, plan local. (Events local would tie the plugin to every project's `.gitignore`.)

# board — a plan-joined build board for Claude Code, across every project

- Status: proposed, 2026-09-15
- Decider: Tanveer Hoque
- Supersedes: `ledgerflow/.local/adr/0001-agent-board.md` (v2) and `ledgerflow/.local/board-spec.md`, which stay as the
  record of how the per-repo version was built and measured.

## 1. What this is

A Claude Code plugin. Hooks report what every agent in every project is doing; a stdlib Node server joins those events to
the project's plan (`PROGRESS.md`: milestones → steps → lanes → boxes) and serves one derived model; a single HTML page
renders it live over SSE and, published as an artifact, renders the same model as a snapshot. A skill teaches the main
thread the text API so it reads the board instead of the files.

Three rules carried over from v2, still load-bearing:

1. **The harness reports, not the agents.** Hooks are the source of every event. Box-level log lines from agents are
   optional refinement, never the signal.
2. **The server owns nothing.** Files are the truth; kill the server and nothing is lost. `PROGRESS.md` has one writer,
   the main thread (by hand or through `POST /tick`). That is what keeps four agents from colliding.
3. **The page parses nothing.** It renders the model and the raw event tail.

## 2. Why this and not one of the existing boards

Surveyed 2026-09-15:

| project | what it is | plan model | why not |
|---|---|---|---|
| [claude-code-kanban](https://github.com/NikiforovAll/claude-code-kanban) | Node + SSE viewer over `~/.claude`, 20k LOC, plugin hooks; waiting badges, UI approvals, board→session doorbell, 17 themes | Claude's native task files (`TaskCreate`), flat, per session, off by default on Opus 5 / Fable 5 | no hierarchy, no lanes, a second writer of plan state next to the markdown |
| [Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor](https://github.com/hoangsonww/Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor) | Express + SQLite + React + WebSockets + Electron + MCP + Codex, 168k LOC, 2,980-line ARCHITECTURE.md, 39 server libs, 18 tables | none — its kanban is agents/sessions by Working · Waiting · Completed; task progress is reduced from `TodoWrite` in transcripts | the plan join would be a new domain (tables, parser, join, tick, React pages) inside a codebase we do not know, diverging from a 1,010-commit upstream we could never pull again |
| [agents-observe](https://github.com/simple10/agents-observe) | Hono + SQLite + React, Docker; hook → HTTP → event stream | none | the same as our Activity tail, with a database and a container |
| [disler observability](https://github.com/disler/claude-code-hooks-multi-agent-observability) | hook → HTTP → WS, swimlanes, pulse chart | none | we have swimlanes |
| agent-platform (ours) | Rust server + iced desktop; processes are created by its planner and approved as a DAG (`/processes/{id}/approve` takes `dag_json`) | its own DAG | no seam to ingest an external run; Claude Code subagents cannot be routed through its proxy; its todos are a product todo board. ADR 0001 rejection stands. |

Every one of them is a generic session or agent monitor. The value here is the join — a box on a lane in a step of a
milestone, with the agent, its commands, its errors and its tokens attributed to it — and none of them has a plan to
join to. Forking the biggest one to add it would cost more than the whole of this, and cut us off from its upstream.

**"Enhance CCAM" without forking:** install it as a plugin next to this one whenever its analytics, cost reports or
notifications are wanted. Hooks are additive; two plugins see the same events. That door stays open. A fork closes it.

Borrowed, with credit: the waiting-state marker and its clearing rule (CCK), the transcript session log (CCK), the
`server.json` beacon (CCK), a per-model price table (CCK, CCAM, governor).

## 3. Shape

### 3.1 Where it lives

`D:/projects/production/ai/plugins/board` — the fourth plugin in the `tanvoid0` marketplace beside governor, crew and
hands. Install once, fires in every project:

```bash
claude plugin install board@tanvoid0
```

### 3.2 Runtime

Node, standard library only (`http`, `fs`, `path`, `os`). No `package.json` dependencies. Reasons: every plugin in the
marketplace is JS; a public hook plugin cannot assume Python on the host; Claude Code itself needs Node, so Node is
always there. The page is one HTML file and ports as-is.

### 3.3 Layout

```
board/
  .claude-plugin/plugin.json      name, version, description
  hooks/hooks.json                the events below, all routed to emit.js
  hooks/emit.js                   hook payload → one JSON line; exit 0 always, never fails the tool call
  server/board.js                 http + SSE + fs.watch; parses the plan, pools the log, joins events, tails transcripts
  server/prices.js                $ per million tokens by model id, four classes; unknown model → null cost
  page/index.html                 the renderer; served by the server and published as the artifact
  skills/board/SKILL.md           the text API and the conventions, for the main thread
  test/fixtures/<project>/        PROGRESS.md · log.md · events.jsonl · transcripts/ · expected summary.txt
  test/check.js                   node test/check.js — builds the model from every fixture, asserts the expected text
  docs/spec.md                    this file
  README.md
```

### 3.4 Data — where every byte goes

| path | writer | content |
|---|---|---|
| `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/.board/server.json` | server | `{"port": 8099, "pid": …}` beacon; written on start, removed on clean exit |
| `~/.claude/.board/<projEnc>/project.json` | `emit.js`, first event for that project | `{"cwd": "D:/projects/…/ledgerflow", "seen": "<iso>"}` |
| `~/.claude/.board/<projEnc>/events.jsonl` | `emit.js` | one JSON object per line, schema in §4 |
| `~/.claude/.board/<projEnc>/model.json` | server, atomic (tmp + rename), ≤ once per 2 s | the derived model, §5 |
| `<cwd>/PROGRESS.md` | main thread only | the plan, grammar in §6 |
| `<cwd>/.local/log.md` | agents (optional), main thread, `POST /log` | box-level lines, §6 |

`projEnc` is Claude Code's own project-directory encoding — every character that is not `[A-Za-z0-9]` becomes `-`
(`D:\projects\practice\microservices\ledgerflow` → `D--projects-practice-microservices-ledgerflow`). Using the same
key means `~/.claude/projects/<projEnc>/` (the transcripts) and `~/.claude/.board/<projEnc>/` (the events) pair by
name, and a session's `transcript_path` locates its project without a lookup.

The plugin writes nothing inside a project. The two project-local files are the user's conventions, edited by the
user's own main thread and agents (through the tick and log routes, or by hand); a project that has neither still
shows up on the board as agents and events, with no plan.

**Project discovery:** every `~/.claude/.board/<projEnc>/` directory. A project is *active* if it has an event in the
last 10 minutes, *recent* within 7 days, else *archived* (listed, not loaded until asked).

**Slug** (what the API and the picker use): the basename of `cwd`; when two projects share a basename, both become
`<parent>-<basename>`. `project.json` records the slug the server assigned so it never changes under a running session.

## 4. Hooks and the event schema

`hooks/hooks.json` registers `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/emit.js"` with a 5 s timeout for:

| hook | matcher | event emitted |
|---|---|---|
| `SessionStart` | — | `session.start` — also writes `project.json` if missing |
| `SessionEnd` | — | `session.end` |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | — | `turn.start` (`prompt` ≤ 200 chars) |
| `Stop` | — | `turn.stop` (the main thread's turn ended; the main is idle now, not "live for 10 more minutes") |
| `SubagentStart` | — | `agent.start` |
| `SubagentStop` | — | `agent.stop` |
| `PreToolUse` | `Bash\|Edit\|Write\|Read\|Grep\|Glob\|NotebookEdit\|Agent` | `tool.pre` |
| `PostToolUse` | `Bash\|Edit\|Write\|NotebookEdit` | `tool.post` |
| `PostToolUseFailure` | `Bash\|Edit\|Write\|NotebookEdit` | `tool.post` with `failed: true` |
| `PermissionRequest` | — | `agent.waiting` (`kind`: `permission`, or `question` for `AskUserQuestion`, `plan` for `ExitPlanMode`) |
| `Notification` | `permission_prompt\|idle_prompt` | `agent.waiting` (`kind`: `permission` / `idle`) — the belt to `PermissionRequest`'s braces; the server dedupes by agent |

`emit.js` is the v2 `emit.py` ported line for line, plus the six new events. It reads `cwd` and `transcript_path` from
the payload (falling back to `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`), derives `projEnc`, appends, exits 0. Every error is swallowed.

**Common fields** on every line: `ts` (UTC ISO ms), `cwd`, `session` (first 8 chars of the session id), `agent`
(17-char agent id, or `main`), `type` (`crew:coder` etc.; `agent` when the id had no type; `main`), `step` (the
`## Current step: N` of `<cwd>/PROGRESS.md`, if any), `ev`.

| `ev` | extra fields |
|---|---|
| `session.start` / `session.end` | — |
| `turn.start` | `prompt` (≤ 200 chars) |
| `turn.stop` | — |
| `agent.start` | `lane` (letter, when the prompt begins `Lane X`), `title` (text after `Lane X —`), `transcript` (absolute path of the subagent transcript — `<dir of transcript_path>/<session_id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, or `agent_transcript_path` when the payload carries it). The prompt is the first user line of that transcript, on disk ~100 ms before the hook fires; retry six times at 50 ms. |
| `agent.stop` | — |
| `agent.waiting` | `kind`, `tool`, `input` (≤ 200 chars of `tool_input`) |
| `tool.pre` | `tool`, `id` (tool_use_id); main thread only: `transcript` (the session transcript); Bash: `cmd` (≤ 400), `desc`; Edit/Write/Read/NotebookEdit: `file` (relative to `cwd`); Grep/Glob: `pattern`, `file`; Agent: `desc`, `subagent`, `lane`, `title` (parsed from the dispatch prompt) |
| `tool.post` | `tool`, `id`, `ms`; Bash: `out`, `err` (last 600 chars each), `interrupted`; a failed call arrives only through `PostToolUseFailure` → `failed: true`, `err` = the error text |

**Waiting is cleared, never toggled off by a hook:** the next `tool.pre`, `tool.post`, `agent.stop` or `turn.stop` by
the same agent clears it in the model. That is CCK's rule and it is the reason the badge cannot stick.

Lane attribution needs the dispatch prompt to start with `Lane X — <name>`. Anything else shows as `?` — honest,
and the signal that a dispatch went out without the convention. Unchanged from v2.

`GET /api/<slug>/model`, SSE `event: model`, and `model.json`. The v2 shape, plus `project`, `waiting`, `say`, `cost`:

```jsonc
      "waiting": {"kind": "permission", "tool": "Bash", "input": "…", "since": "iso"} | null,   // NEW
      "say": "<last assistant text, ≤ 300 chars>" | null,                                        // NEW
      "model": "claude-sonnet-5" | null, "calls": 12,
      "in": 90000, "cw": 30000, "cr": 400000, "out": 4321,                                        // in/cw/cr NEW (Σ per class)
      "ctx": 58000, "ctxPct": 29,

```

Rules, unchanged from v2 unless marked:

- **agent → lane**: `agent.start.lane`; else the nearest earlier `tool.pre` with `tool == "Agent"` in the same
  session whose `lane` is set and not yet claimed; else `null`. `story` = the story owning that letter (current step
  first, then sandboxes). The main thread is lane `C` when the current step has one.
- **task status**: ticked → `done`; else by its last log line: `done` → `reported`, `blocked` → `blocked`,
  `start`/`note` → `doing`; else `todo`. A parent with children: `done` only if ticked; else `blocked` if any child is
  blocked, `doing` if any child is doing/reported, else its own log-derived status. Counts include every depth.
- **task agent / times**: `agent` = label of the `start` line (else `done`); a label matches an agent when it equals
  the type, the lane letter, the id or its last five chars, or `main`. `started` = first `start` ts (or the agent's start
  when the lane's agent is live and the task is `doing` with no lines); `finished` = last `done`; `ms` accordingly.
- **tool attribution**: the `start` line for KEY by label L opens a window closing at L's next later line that is
  another key's `start` or this key's `done`/`blocked`; `tool.pre` by a matching agent on that lane inside the window
  counts (`tools`; `errors` = `tool.post` with `err`, `failed` or `interrupted`).
- **live**: a subagent with `agent.start`, no `agent.stop`, last event < 30 min. **NEW:** `main@sess` is live from
  `turn.start`/`session.start` until `turn.stop`/`session.end`, with the 10-minute silence rule kept as the fallback for a
  session whose hooks predate this version.
- **NEW waiting**: set by `agent.waiting`; cleared by the agent's next `tool.pre` / `tool.post` / `agent.stop` /
  `turn.stop`; a `waiting` agent is still `live`.
- **Transcript tail** (per `transcript` path seen; byte offset kept in memory, whole file on first sight; dedupe
  `message.id`): `model` (last), `calls`, Σ of all four usage classes (**NEW**: `in`, `cw`, `cr` alongside `out`), `ctx`
  = the latest message's input + cache_creation + cache_read, `window` = 200 000 or 1 000 000 once any message exceeded
  200 000, `ctxPct`. **NEW** `say`: the last `text` block of the last `assistant` message, ≤ 300 chars, whitespace
  collapsed — what the agent is saying between tool calls.
- **NEW cost**: `prices.js` = `{ "<model id>": {in, cw, cr, out} }` in USD per million; `cost` = Σ class × price;
  unknown model → `null`, never a guess. Values are entered from the claude-api skill reference at build time and dated
  in a comment; governor's ratio weights (`input 0.2 · cacheWrite 0.25 · cacheRead 0.02` of output) are the sanity
  check, not the source.

## 6. The plan and the log — grammar, unchanged

`PROGRESS.md`:

```

## Milestones
### M1 — Name ✅
- [x] 01 Step title (`3237c3a`)          ← optional commit hash in backticks anywhere on the line
- [ ] 16 Step title — **current**
## Current step: 16 — Title
Done when: …(one paragraph; ends at the first blank line)…
Decisions taken before the lanes (keep consistent):
- …(markdown until the first ### Lane)…
### Lane R — risk-service · parallel · one agent
_touches: `services/risk-service/**`, `pom.xml`_
- [x] R1 box text (markdown inline)
- [ ] R5 box text
```

Lane heading parts after `·` are tags; one is the mode: `serial | parallel | inline | optional`.

`.local/log.md`: `- <UTC ISO> · <agent label> · <KEY or lane letter> · start|done|blocked|note · <one line>` under
`## step NN` / `## sandbox` headings. Lines under the current step's and sandbox headings form one pool; the key decides
which story a line joins; older sections are ignored. Only events with `step == current` are joined.

Both files are the user's. The plugin ships the grammar in `SKILL.md` and a fixture, nothing else.

## 7. Server and API

`node server/board.js [--port 8099] [--check]` — `ThreadingHTTPServer`'s equivalent: one `http.createServer`, binds
`127.0.0.1`, silenced access log, `fs.watch` on every `~/.claude/.board/<projEnc>/` (recursive where the platform
allows, 1 s stat poll where not — Windows `fs.watch` on directories is fine; on Linux `recursive` needs Node 20) and on
each loaded project's `PROGRESS.md` and `.local/log.md`. Model rebuilt on demand from cached snapshots (mtime/size),
one lock, malformed JSONL lines ignored. Writes the beacon on start; removes it on SIGINT/SIGTERM when the pid is its own.

| route | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `GET /` | the page; `?p=<slug>` preselects a project |
| `GET /api/projects` | text: one line per project — `ledgerflow · active · 2 live · step 17 (5/19) · 3s ago`; `?format=json` |
| `GET /api/<slug>/model` | the derived model |
| `GET /api/<slug>/state` | `{"model", "events": [last 5000], "now"}` — the page's first load |
| `GET /api/<slug>/stream` | SSE: `event: model` on any input change (debounce 300 ms; at least every 5 s while any agent is live), `event: events` (new lines), `event: ping` every 15 s |
| `GET /api/<slug>/summary` | text ≤ 25 lines: `project: ledgerflow` · status line · per story, per lane: `lane R risk-service · parallel · 8/9 · live crew:coder@a1b2c (sonnet 5, ctx 29%, $1.87) on R5.1 · last: <cmd 80> (12s ago)`; `WAITING permission: Bash …` on the lane line when set; then `blocked:`, `reported (awaiting tick):`, `next:` |
| `GET /api/<slug>/next[?n=3]` | text: Done-when, then the next `n` todo tasks per lane, key + full text |
| `GET /api/<slug>/wip` | text: live agents only — id suffix, type, model, ctx%, $, lane, box, elapsed, waiting, `say`, last 3 commands/files with ms and `ERR`, error count |
| `GET /api/<slug>/lane/{X}` | text: heading, tags, touches, task tree by depth |
| `GET /api/<slug>/task/{KEY}` | text: breadcrumb, status, text, agent/model, times, log lines, children, last 20 attributed tool events |
| `GET /api/<slug>/agent/{id or suffix}` | text: the agent block + `say` + last 30 events |
| `POST /api/<slug>/tick` | `{"key": "R3", "done": true}` → flips the checkbox in `<cwd>/PROGRESS.md` (first match, any indent), rewrites `(N / M boxes)` in the Status line, answers with the summary. 404 if the key is absent |
| `POST /api/<slug>/log` | `{"agent", "key", "status", "note"}` → appends the line to `<cwd>/.local/log.md` under the last heading |
| `POST /api/<slug>/export` | `{"dir": "<absolute path>"}` → writes `index.html`, `model.json`, `events.jsonl` there; answers with the exact `Artifact(...)` call to make. This is how a snapshot gets published from a directory the Artifact tool may read (the caller's scratchpad), without the plugin ever writing into a repo |
| `GET /api/summary` etc. (no slug) | the most recently active project; first line names it. Keeps the old curl lines working until a CLAUDE.local.md is updated |
| every text route | `?format=json` |

Text rules as before: for Claude to read in one tool call — no tables, no markdown headers, one fact per line, `hh:mm:ss`
absolute, `12s ago` / `3m` / `1.2h` relative, ≤ 60 lines except `task` and `agent`.

`--check`: loads every `test/fixtures/<project>/`, builds the model with `now` pinned to the fixture's `now.txt`,
diffs `summary` against `expected/summary.txt` and `wip` against `expected/wip.txt`, exits non-zero on any diff.
That is the one runnable check; no framework.

## 8. Page

`page/index.html`, the v2 page ported unchanged where nothing changed, plus:

- **Project picker** in the header: `GET /api/projects`, badge per project (`● 2 live`, `⏸ waiting`), remembered in
  `localStorage`, `?p=` in the URL. Snapshot mode has no picker — one project per artifact.
- **Waiting**: amber card border and an amber chip `waiting · permission · Bash` on the agent badge and the lane
  header; the agent row in the Agents panel shows `since`.
- **Say**: one muted line under the agent's last command in the Agents panel and in the Detail sidebar — what the agent
  said last. Generation time is still invisible; this shows the last thing that landed.
- **Cost**: `$` next to tokens on agent badges, lane headers (Σ agents on the lane) and the totals bar.
- Two modes, same file: `location.protocol === "http:"` → `state` + `EventSource(stream)`, live dot on; else
  `fetch("model.json")` + `fetch("events.jsonl")` once, live dot off. First line `<meta charset="utf-8">`, then
  `<title>`; no `<html>/<head>/<body>`; only external script `marked` 4.3.0 from cdnjs; fonts from Google Fonts with a
  real fallback stack; everything else inline; works at 400 px.

Not on the page: themes, keyboard shortcut sheets, approvals, storage manager. It is a viewer.

## 9. Skill — `skills/board/SKILL.md`

Replaces the "Reading the board" and "Ticking" blocks of a project's `CLAUDE.local.md`. It tells the main thread:

- server up? `curl -s localhost:8099/api/projects` — if it fails: `(node "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/server/board.js" > ~/.claude/.board/server.log 2>&1 &)` and retry. The beacon at `~/.claude/.board/server.json` says the port.
- session start / "where are we": `curl -s localhost:8099/api/<slug>/summary`
- before dispatching: `/next`; while agents run: `/wip`; one lane, task, agent: `/lane/X`, `/task/KEY`, `/agent/ID`.
- tick without opening the file: `curl -s -XPOST localhost:8099/api/<slug>/tick -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"key":"R3","done":true}'` — main thread only, same turn the report lands.
- publish: `curl -s -XPOST localhost:8099/api/<slug>/export -d '{"dir":"<scratchpad>/board"}'` then the `Artifact(...)`
  call it prints, with the project's artifact `url`.
- the lane-prompt convention: first line `Lane X — <name>`; last paragraph the verbatim log-line instruction; agents
  never touch `PROGRESS.md`.
- the grammar of §6, and the "expanding a step into lanes" rules (disjoint file sets, modes, ≤ 4 agents, boxes name a
  file or a command).

Per project, `CLAUDE.local.md` keeps only what is project-specific: the slug, the artifact URL, the step-file source.

At a step boundary (17 → 18), in this order:

1. Install the plugin; start the new server on a different port (8100) beside the old one.
2. `mkdir ~/.claude/.board/D--projects-practice-microservices-ledgerflow && cp .local/events.jsonl` there (the old lines
   have no `cwd`; the server takes the directory as the project).
3. Compare `/api/ledgerflow/summary` (8100) with `/api/summary` (8099). Identical → continue.
4. Remove the `hooks` block from `.claude/settings.local.json` (otherwise every event is written twice); stop 8099;
   restart the new server on 8099.
5. `CLAUDE.local.md`: replace the reading/ticking/publishing blocks with the slug and the artifact URL; the skill has
   the rest. `.local/`: delete `board.py`, `hooks/`, `progress.html`, `model.json`, `events.jsonl`; keep `log.md`,
   `adr/`, `board-spec.md` (history).
6. Republish through `export`; the artifact URL is unchanged.

## 12. Ceilings, named

- The artifact is a snapshot per republish. The hosted page cannot reach `localhost`.
- One Node process per hook (~50 ms) — the same class as governor's gate; two per Bash/Edit/Write; noticeable on
  Read-heavy agents, acceptable. No batching, no daemon.
- Generation time stays invisible; `say` shows the last thing that landed, not what is being written.
- A killed agent never gets `agent.stop`; it ages out after 30 min. A main thread whose `Stop` hook is lost ages out
  after 10 min.
- `events.jsonl` grows ~1 line per tool call. Rotate at a step boundary (`events.jsonl` → `events.<step>.jsonl`; the
  server reads only the live file). The page loads the last 5000 lines.
- `turn.start.prompt` puts the first 200 chars of every user prompt into a file that gets published as an artifact
  snapshot. Artifacts are private by default; the export route accepts `"prompts": false` to strip them.
- Keys must not repeat across a step and a sandbox that are open at once.
- `fs.watch` semantics differ per platform; the 1 s stat poll is the fallback and the SSE debounce hides it.

## 13. Not doing

SQLite, React, Electron, web push, themes, approvals from the board (the desktop app has that UI), the board→session
doorbell (the main thread already receives every subagent's report), Codex, Claude's native task tools as the plan,
authentication (binds `127.0.0.1`), a hosted mode.

input.content:
# Plan layer — a plan-joined build board on top of Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor

- Status: proposed, 2026-09-15
- Decider: Tanveer Hoque
- Base: fork of [hoangsonww/Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor](https://github.com/hoangsonww/Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor) at
  `3a7630b` (v2.2.0, 2026-09-13). This working tree has it as remote `upstream`.
- Supersedes: `ledgerflow/.local/adr/0001-agent-board.md` (v2) and `ledgerflow/.local/board-spec.md`, which stay as the
  record of how the per-repo board was built and what was measured.

## 1. Decision

Fork CCAM. Keep everything it already does — sessions, agents, events, tokens and cost, waiting badges, WebSocket
push, SQLite, the React UI, the Electron shell, the hook installer — and add one thing on top: **the plan join**.
A project's `PROGRESS.md` (milestones → steps → lanes → boxes) becomes a page where every box shows the agent on it,
what it ran, what failed, what it cost; and a text API the main thread reads instead of the files.

Why fork rather than build (the earlier draft said build): the requirement is a proper UI and a database, across every
project. CCAM has both, plus a year of edge cases in hook ingestion and transcript parsing we would otherwise
re-discover. What it lacks is exactly one domain, ours, and that domain is additive.

Why it is viable — checked in the source, not the README:

| we need | CCAM has | where |
|---|---|---|
| every project, every session | hooks installed in `~/.claude/settings.json`; `sessions.cwd` | `scripts/install-hooks.js`, `server/db.js:163` |
| subagents with their prompt | `agents` row per `Agent` dispatch; `agents.task` = first 500 chars of the prompt — `Lane X — name` is in there | `server/routes/hooks.js:418-456` |
| tool events with I/O | `events(session_id, agent_id, event_type, tool_name, summary, data)` | `server/db.js:195` |
| tokens and $ | `token_usage` per session × model; `model_pricing`; `transcript-cache.js` extracts `tokensByModel` from any transcript path | `server/db.js:208,243`, `server/lib/transcript-cache.js` |
| waiting-for-user | `agents.status = 'waiting'`, `Notification` + `UserPromptSubmit` hooks | `server/routes/hooks.js:52-106` |
| live push | `broadcast(type, data)` server side, `useWebSocket(onMessage)` client side | `server/websocket.js:62`, `client/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts:79` |
| a place for a page | react-router `Routes` in `App.tsx`, nav array in `Sidebar.tsx`, components (`StatusBadge`, `AgentCard`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState`, `StatCard`) | `client/src/App.tsx:126-141`, `client/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:99` |
| tests without a framework | `node --test server/__tests__/*.test.js`; client vitest | `package.json` |

And the gap that is not additive, found in `server/routes/hooks.js`:

> "Subagent tool_use blocks never fire hooks on the parent session — this scan is the only path that attributes them
> to the subagent's agent_id." (`hooks.js:1224`)

That was true once; it is not now. `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` fire inside subagents and carry `agent_id` +
`agent_type` (probed 2026-09-15, Claude Code 2.1.238 — ledgerflow ADR 0001). CCAM does not read `data.agent_id` on
tool hooks, does not install `SubagentStart`, gives each subagent its own `uuidv4()`, attributes live tool events to
the "deepest working agent" and matches `SubagentStop` by name prefix → `subagent_type` → prompt → oldest working.
With three `crew:coder`s on three lanes that is wrong while they run and repaired only by the JSONL scan at stop. The
plan join needs it right live. So the fork carries **one patch in upstream files** (§4.1), written so it can go
upstream as a pull request — it is a bug there too — and the rest lives in new files.

## 2. Fork strategy — keep the pull open

- `upstream` = hoangsonww; `origin` = the fork. Track upstream release tags; rebase `main` onto each.
- Everything of ours lives under `server/plan/`, `server/routes/plans.js`, `client/src/plan/`, `docs/plan-layer.md`,
  `test/fixtures/plan/`. Upstream files are touched in exactly the places listed in §6 — a one-line require, a
  one-line `app.use`, a route, a nav item, a locale block, one migration, and the ingest patch.
- The ingest patch is opened upstream as a PR the week it lands. Once merged, the diff in upstream files is six lines.
- Not renamed, not rebranded. `ccam` stays `ccam`; the plan page is a page.

## 3. Start using it today — before any code

```bash
# on GitHub: fork hoangsonww/Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor under tanvoid0 (the user does this; it creates a public repo)
cd D:/projects/production/ai/agentic-ai/agent-monitor
git remote add origin git@github.com:tanvoid0/Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor.git
npm install                    # Node ≥ 22.22 (24.14 here); node:sqlite, no native build
npm run build                  # client → dist
node scripts/install-hooks.js  # writes the hook block into ~/.claude/settings.json — every project from now on
npm start                      # http://localhost:4820
```

From that moment: every session in every project, its agents, tool events, waiting state, tokens and $ — the
Dashboard, Sessions, Activity and Analytics pages. That already replaces the Agents and Activity panels of the v2 board.
Ledgerflow's own hooks keep running beside it until §8; both write, nothing collides (different files, different ports).

## 4. What we add

### 4.1 The ingest patch (upstream files)

1. `scripts/install-hooks.js:87-94` — add `SubagentStart` to `HOOKS_WITHOUT_MATCHER`. It carries `agent_id`,
   `agent_type`, `session_id`, and the subagent transcript is on disk ~100 ms before it fires.
2. `server/db.js` migration — `ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN claude_agent_id TEXT` + index. Pattern at `db.js:557`.
3. `server/routes/hooks.js`:
   - `SubagentStart`: bind. Find the most recent `working` subagent in the session with `claude_agent_id IS NULL`
     and matching `subagent_type` (else any unbound); set `claude_agent_id`; record the transcript path in
     `metadata.transcript_path` (from `agent_transcript_path`, or derived `<dir of transcript_path>/<session_id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`).
     No unbound row (a dispatch the `Agent` hook missed) → insert one.
   - `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` / `PostToolUseFailure` / `Notification` with `data.agent_id`: attribute to the row
     with that `claude_agent_id`. Only when absent fall back to today's deepest-working heuristic.
   - `SubagentStop` with `data.agent_id`: match by `claude_agent_id` first; the four heuristics stay as fallback.
   - The JSONL scan at stop stays — it back-fills anything the hooks missed and older sessions.
4. Tests: `server/__tests__/hooks-agent-id.test.js` — three concurrent subagents of the same type, tool events
   interleaved, each lands on its own row; stop matches by id.

~80 lines. This is the PR.

### 4.2 Data

Two tables, in `server/plan/schema.js`, created from one call added to `db.js`'s init:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plans (
  cwd        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,           -- the project; sessions.cwd joins here
  slug       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,       -- basename of cwd; parent-basename on collision; never changes once set
  source     TEXT NOT NULL,              -- PROGRESS.md as last read
  parsed     TEXT NOT NULL,              -- JSON: milestones, stories, lanes, tasks (structure + ticks only)
  step       INTEGER,                    -- ## Current step: N
  mtime      TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now'))
);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plan_log (
  id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  cwd        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES plans(cwd) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  step       INTEGER NOT NULL,           -- the step the line belongs to; keys repeat across steps
  key        TEXT NOT NULL,              -- R5.1, or a lane letter
  agent      TEXT NOT NULL,              -- label: crew:coder, a lane letter, an id suffix, main
  status     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(status IN ('start','done','blocked','note')),
  note       TEXT,
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ','now'))
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_plan_log_cwd_step ON plan_log(cwd, step);
```

What stays a file: **`<cwd>/PROGRESS.md`** — the plan is authored as markdown because a main thread expanding a step
writes twenty boxes in markdown far better than in twenty API calls. Writers: the main thread (expanding a step) and
the server (`tick` flips a checkbox). Agents never. **`.local/log.md` is retired**: box-level lines go to `plan_log`
through `POST /api/plans/:slug/log`. A `<cwd>/.local/log.md` that exists is imported read-only (same grammar) so a
project mid-flight keeps its history.

Discovery: no registration. The watcher (`server/plan/watcher.js`, `fs.watch` with a 2 s stat fallback, the pattern
of `server/lib/cc-watcher.js`) checks `<cwd>/PROGRESS.md` for every distinct `sessions.cwd` seen in the last 7 days;
present → upsert `plans`, watch the file; changed → re-parse, `broadcast("plan_updated", {slug})`.

### 4.4 The join — `server/plan/join.js`

Input: `plans.parsed` + `plan_log` for the current step + CCAM's `sessions`, `agents`, `events` for that `cwd` +
per-agent transcript figures. Output: the v2 model shape (below), computed on request, cached per `cwd` until any
input changes (a `sessions`/`agents`/`events` write for that cwd, a `plan_log` insert, a plan re-parse, a transcript
mtime).

- **agent → lane**: `agents.task` begins `Lane X` → lane `X`, title after `—`; else the dispatching `Agent` event's
  `tool_input.prompt` (`events.data`) in the same session, first unclaimed match; else `null`. `story` = the story
  owning that letter (current step first, then sandboxes). Main thread (`agents.type = 'main'`) is lane `C` when the
  step has one.
- **task status**: ticked → `done`; else by its last `plan_log` line: `done` → `reported`, `blocked` → `blocked`,
  `start`/`note` → `doing`; else `todo`. Parent with children: `done` only if ticked; else `blocked` if any child is,
  `doing` if any child is doing/reported, else its own. Counts include every depth.
- **task agent / times**: label of the `start` line (else `done`); a label matches an agent when it equals
  `subagent_type`, the lane letter, `claude_agent_id` or its last five chars, or `main`. `started` = first `start`
  (or the agent's `started_at` when the lane's agent is working and the task is `doing` with no lines);
  `finished` = last `done`; `ms` accordingly.
- **tool attribution**: the `start` for KEY by label L opens a window closing at L's next later line that is another
  key's `start` or this key's `done`/`blocked`; `events` rows with `event_type = 'PreToolUse'` by a matching agent on
  that lane inside the window count (`tools`; `errors` = the paired post event with stderr, `failed`, or interrupted).
- **live**: `agents.status = 'working'` (CCAM's own rule, now correct per agent after §4.1); `waiting` =
  `agents.status = 'waiting'` with the `Notification` payload's kind and tool.
- **per-agent figures** (`server/plan/tail.js`, the v2 tailer): from `metadata.transcript_path` (subagents) or
  `sessions.transcript_path` (main) — `transcriptCache.extract()` for `tokensByModel`/`latestModel`; our own tail for
  `ctx` (latest message's input + cache_creation + cache_read), `window` (200k, or 1M once exceeded), `ctxPct`, and
  `say` (last assistant text block, ≤ 300 chars). `cost` = `tokensByModel` × `model_pricing` — CCAM's table, CCAM's
  rates, so the plan page and the Analytics page agree to the cent.

| route | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `GET /` | projects with a plan: slug, cwd, step, counts, live agents, last event age (JSON; `?format=text` one line each) |
| `GET /:slug/model` | the model |
| `GET /:slug/summary` | **text/plain** ≤ 25 lines: `project: ledgerflow` · status · per lane: `lane D Demo · serial · 0/6 · live crew:coder@54a7d (sonnet 5, ctx 52%, $1.87) on D1 · WAITING permission Bash · last: <cmd 80> (3s ago)` · `blocked:` · `reported (awaiting tick):` · `next:` |

| `GET /:slug/wip` | text: live agents — id suffix, type, model, ctx%, $, lane, box, elapsed, waiting, say, last 3 commands with ms and `ERR` |
| `GET /:slug/lane/:X` · `/:slug/task/:key` · `/:slug/agent/:id` | text, as v2 |
| `POST /:slug/tick` `{"key","done"}` | flips the checkbox in `<cwd>/PROGRESS.md` (first match, any indent), rewrites `(N / M boxes)` in the Status line, re-parses, answers with the summary. 404 unknown key. The UI's checkbox calls the same route |
| `POST /:slug/log` `{"agent","key","status","note"}` | inserts a `plan_log` row for the current step; `broadcast("plan_log", …)` |
| `POST /:slug/export` `{"dir","prompts": true}` | writes `index.html` (the v2 snapshot page, kept at `server/plan/snapshot.html`), `model.json`, `events.jsonl` (last 5000 events of the project, v2 line shape) into `dir` and answers with the exact `Artifact(...)` call. | every text route | `?format=json` |

- Status: proposed, 2026-09-15
- Decider: Tanveer Hoque
- Base: fork of [hoangsonww/Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor](https://github.com/hoangsonww/Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor) at

Fork CCAM. Keep everything it already does — sessions, agents, events, tokens and cost, waiting badges, WebSocket
push, SQLite, the React UI, the Electron shell, the hook installer — and add one thing on top: **the plan join**.
A project's `PROGRESS.md` (milestones → steps → lanes → boxes) becomes a page where every box shows the agent on it,
what it ran, what failed, what it cost; and a text API the main thread reads instead of the files.

Why fork rather than build (the earlier draft said build): the requirement is a proper UI and a database, across every
project. CCAM has both, plus a year of edge cases in hook ingestion and transcript parsing we would otherwise
re-discover. What it lacks is exactly one domain, ours, and that domain is additive.

| we need | CCAM has | where |

| tokens and $ | `token_usage` per session × model; `model_pricing`; `transcript-cache.js` extracts `tokensByModel` from any transcript path | `server/db.js:208,243`, `server/lib/transcript-cache.js` |
| waiting-for-user | `agents.status = 'waiting'`, `Notification` + `UserPromptSubmit` hooks | `server/routes/hooks.js:52-106` |

| a place for a page | react-router `Routes` in `App.tsx`, nav array in `Sidebar.tsx`, components (`StatusBadge`, `AgentCard`, `Skeleton`, `EmptyState`, `StatCard`) | `client/src/App.tsx:126-141`, `client/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:99` |
